title: Vaccine-associated paralytic poliomyelitis: a case report of flaccid monoparesis after oral polio vaccine.
ehr_evidence: Data source was direct clinical assessment, physical examination, laboratory tests, MRI, and electrodiagnostic evaluations on a single patient.
summary: Case report describing a 4-month-old male infant in Korea who developed acute flaccid paralysis and persistent hypotonic monoparesis following oral polio vaccine administration.
key_findings: First clinically confirmed case of vaccine-associated paralytic poliomyelitis (VAPP) in Korea.
Flaccid paralysis developed 4 weeks after OPV immunization.
Virus isolation from stool and CSF failed.
Persistent hypotonic monoparesis and atrophy remained after 18 months of rehabilitation therapy.
limitations: failed to isolate causative virus strain
diagnosis relied on clinical criteria without virological confirmation
